correctness.rationale: Cut vectors span all edge coordinates via 2e_uv=delta(u)+delta(v)-delta({u,v}). Switching averages every feasible Minkowski center to h=1/2 and turns each reflected cut into the same diagonal point t1. MaxCut upper bound and edge-transitive orbit averaging match at t=M/m>1/2. At the optimum the tight total-edge supporting inequality after every cut switching forces every Walsh coefficient z_e of any alternative center to vanish, establishing unique center. Separate-affinity of multipartite MaxCut in the class occupancy proves a^2 floor(r^2/4) and the closed parity law. Exact finite script outputs are reproducible but not taken as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The claim completely determines a classical affine-invariant geometric quantity and its unique center for every edge-transitive cut polytope, bypassing exponential facet enumeration and linking the coefficient exactly to the classical MaxCut graph invariant. The explicit infinite balanced multipartite family shows the invariant depends only on parity and number of parts, not blowup size despite rapidly growing dimension. For non-K5-minor-free complete graphs it gives arbitrarily large asymmetry, so it is not a routine subcase of the prior minor-free odd-girth classification. Its complete classification and symmetry-to-optimization bridge motivate the exact invariant rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
